turns.assessment: The correlated one-second errors on both ends of och114 and the brief protection excursion of svc169 indicate a transient on the working lightpath shared with svc183. Stable power, OSNR, BER, DGD, amplifier, and pump measurements strongly oppose a persistent amplifier, fibre-loss, WSS, or line-card failure. A fast SOP transient on the aerial S13-S23 cable best fits, but the observations do not distinguish its two directional span representations, and they do not substantiate a continuing loss after the transient.

proposals.rationale: E59 is the aerial span in the S15-to-S08 direction of och114. A millisecond polarization transient can produce the observed errored second and protection reaction without a detectable change in sampled optical metrics.
E99 is the reverse-direction representation of the same aerial S13-S23 cable section. Errors were recorded at both och114 receivers, so the available evidence cannot select E99 over E59.
Brief handling or movement of the aerial span could cause a short hit, but a power excursion would be more expected than the completely stable optical measurements.
The reverse fibre could likewise have experienced a brief mechanical disturbance, although the lack of observed power movement makes this less likely than an SOP-only transient.
A svc183 client-port failure could explain an ongoing customer-specific loss, but it would not explain the simultaneous och114 errors and svc169 protection activity.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
